PullRequest.Title: Cheaper diff scrolling: no forced layouts in the hunk toolbars, no layer per +/- sign
PullRequest.Body: fyi @hediet --- Scrolling a side-by-side diff did work on every frame beyond its two editors. Two small fixes, one commit each: - **Hunk toolbars.** The gutter between the editors read its own height on every scroll event, and each hunk's toolbar read its buttons' height right after the gutter moved it, so every hunk in view forced a layout on every scroll event. The gutter now reads its height when it resizes, and a toolbar measures its buttons once, and again when it's rebuilt or its items change. - **+/- signs.** `opacity: 0.7` made the rasterizer draw each sign in the margins through a layer of its own, on every frame that scrolls. Dimming the glyph to 70% of its color on `::before`, where `currentColor` is the sign's own color, draws them the same, within 6/255 in a color channel. This came up while making diffs scroll quickly with the editorView GPU editor (#336479). Both fixes help the DOM editor too. ## Measurements Scrolling a diff of `textModel.ts` (113 hunks), one wheel event a frame. The gutter forced 7.07 layouts per frame, and now 0.17: a toolbar measures its buttons when its hunk scrolls into view. Alternating old and new in one instance over 8 rounds, busy time per frame: | | editorView GPU editor | DOM editor | |---|---|---| | Hunk toolbars: renderer main thread | −0.38 ms (6/8 rounds lower) | −0.23 ms (6/8) | | +/- signs: GPU process | −0.31 ms (8/8) | −0.20 ms (7/8) | ## Screenshot changes The screenshot check flags 12 diff-editor fixtures. In all of them, only the +/- signs change: every + sign changes the same 36 pixels and every − sign the same 10, by at most 6/255 in a color channel. Nothing else moves or changes color. Before, each sign was drawn into a layer of its own and blended at 70%; now its glyph is drawn straight in a 70% color, which blends slightly differently. All 12 screenshots, with the changed pixels in magenta: The signs zoomed 12×: before, after, the changed pixels, and the difference 40× brighter: ## How to verify - `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/widget/diffEditorWidget.test.ts`: the new `EditorGutter` test fails without the change (the gutter reads its height on each of 10 scrolls). - Record scrolling a diff in DevTools' Performance panel: no forced reflows from `EditorGutter.render`, and from `DiffToolBar.layout` only when a hunk scrolls into view. - Hunk toolbars sit where they did, also after selecting across a hunk. The +/- signs look as on `main` in a dark, a light and a high-contrast theme, with `icon.foreground` customized, in an inline diff, and in a notebook diff with a cell selected. 🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Repeated synchronous clientHeight reads after per-hunk top/height writes force browser layout on the scroll critical path. Previously each laid-out visible hunk made two height reads per scroll, plus one gutter-height read per render; the first hunk read follows geometry writes and the second can follow toolbar reconstruction.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Strongly evidenced synchronous layout work on each scroll, scaling with visible hunk layout invocations and scroll-event frequency, consumes renderer main-thread time and risks scroll jank. This is static call-path evidence; no benchmark timings were independently measured.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Warm scrolling reuses one height per live toolbar and one height per gutter; toolbar measurement occurs on creation, reconstruction, menu change, or retry of a zero result, and gutter measurement occurs at construction and resize. Offscreen views are disposed, so cached state remains bounded by visible hunks.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base line 291 reads buttons.clientHeight inside DiffToolBar.layout, and base line 294 repeats that read after _isSmall may rebuild the toolbar. EditorGutter.render is synchronously subscribed to editor.onDidScrollChange and, for each intersecting visible hunk, writes view.domNode.style.top and style.height immediately before calling that layout method. Thus the base implementation crosses a synchronous browser layout boundary after geometry writes for each laid-out hunk on every scroll. The new line 300 uses a cached nonzero height, invalidated only on toolbar reconstruction (254) and menu-item change (278). The companion gutter change replaces the per-render clientHeight read at base editorGutter.ts:86 with initialization/ResizeObserver measurements. The added test asserts ten scroll-triggered layouts with zero gutter-height reads. Blame identifies b7d35c8bdddeb7d4bfebf81cb6733b4a5ee06aa9 as introducing both base height-read paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll a side-by-side text diff with hunk toolbars enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: onDidScrollChange synchronously updates the scroll observable and runs EditorGutter.render. Visible hunk DOM positions and DiffToolBar.layout must finish before the renderer can present the updated gutter.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser layout through clientHeight after gutter or per-hunk DOM mutations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one gutter-height read and two toolbar-height reads for each of K layout invocations. After: zero gutter-height reads during scrolling and at most one initial nonzero measurement per distinct newly created or invalidated toolbar; zero toolbar-height reads on ordinary warm scrolling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The gutter measured on every render and each toolbar measured immediately after its parent top/height writes. This creates repeated layout work on the scroll critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous geometry reads can flush browser layout and block frame presentation. The diff removes those reads from warm scrolling rather than adding them.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll-event frequency; total diff mappings examined by the unchanged provider; K visible-range/hunk intersections laid out per event. Views are deduplicated by hunk id, so V distinct visible views retain V cached numbers, even when K exceeds V.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer-thread execution; observable transactions group updates but do not parallelize the visible-hunk loop. No added tasks, global fan-out, or external concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The gutter height is cached per EditorGutter. Each visible DiffToolBar caches a nonzero buttons height for its lifetime. Cold entry measures a newly created toolbar; warm scrolling reuses its height. Rebuilt toolbars and changed menu items invalidate that cache; zero results are retried. Offscreen views are deleted and disposed, not accumulated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the scroll subscription, per-hunk writes followed by layout, deleted geometry reads, new cache, and disposal paths are directly traced. The regression fix was recorded with blame provenance.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual frame-time savings depend on visible hunk count, DOM complexity, and browser layout invalidation. No timings were independently measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression. The diff removes synchronous layout reads on the warm scrolling path; existing all-mapping scans and offscreen recreation are not newly amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct, resize, hide, reveal, or relayout a diff editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction seeds the gutter height. The existing ResizeObserver updates it and triggers gutter rendering after a size change; rendering and any cold toolbar measurements precede presentation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure gutter clientHeight at construction and in the existing ResizeObserver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial read per gutter and one read per resize delivery. Constructor placement can perform one read before a model exists, where the old render would return without measuring.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No explicit construction measurement. Attached-model renders measured once, including renders triggered by resize, scroll, view-zone changes, and content-size changes. The diff relocates measurement to construction and resize instead of adding an observer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial read is on widget construction; resize reads are in the existing resize callback. Subsequent renders reuse the result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create visible toolbar DOM and initialize the local MenuWorkbenchToolBar; synchronously measure newly created toolbar buttons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One creation and cold height measurement per distinct visible toolbar after initial display or re-entry. The number of views remains viewport-bounded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same visible views and local menus were constructed; button height was measured twice per layout rather than once and cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Visible toolbar creation and its initial measurement must complete for the gutter to display. No additional menu construction is caused by the height cache.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One gutter per instantiated diff widget; resize deliveries per live widget; the distinct visible toolbars entering after reveal. Embedded notebook editors can initially have zero dimensions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Constructor work is synchronous. ResizeObserver delivery uses the browser's existing scheduling and a synchronous observable transaction; the observer is not newly introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The gutter cache is refreshed at construction and every ResizeObserver callback. A zero gutter height suppresses rendering until a size update. A zero toolbar measurement is deliberately not treated as a usable warm cache value. ResizeObserver is disconnected on disposal, and the DisposableMap owns and disposes views.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cache ownership, scheduling, and before/after read placement; no evidence of added unbounded initialization work or retained resources.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The one construction read is moved earlier, including for model-less widgets; its duration depends on pending browser layout. It is bounded per widget and does not establish a realistic scaling regression over the existing initialization and eventual rendering path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. A bounded initial geometry read supports the scrolling optimization, resize uses the existing observer, and lifecycle cleanup is preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move the cursor, select across hunks, or update hunk-toolbar menu items.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable cursor/selection changes update gutter items. Menu-id or small-toolbar changes rebuild the toolbar synchronously; local menu-change handling updates actions then calls layout for the last range.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rebuild menu/action DOM and read toolbar clientHeight after menu contents change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing rebuilds per affected live toolbar; one measurement following each invalidation and layout. The diff does not increase rebuild count or item count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same rebuild and relayout paths existed, with two height reads per layout. Menu lookup, action-view creation, and action execution are not newly invoked by invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Toolbar rebuilding and measurement remain on the visible update path; subsequent layouts benefit from the cached value.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct visible hunk toolbars; one combined selection toolbar when selected range mappings are present; actual menu changes, rather than every scroll or every total mapping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer-thread observables and existing menu events; no new parallel requests or queue. MenuWorkbenchToolBar updates its DOM before firing the menu-items event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Toolbar reconstruction explicitly clears the height cache before creating MenuWorkbenchToolBar. onDidChangeMenuItems clears it before relayout. One cached number is owned by each live toolbar; old views and their toolbar stores are disposed. Menu/action lookup remains local and unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reconstruction dependencies, menu event ordering, invalidation, and bounded view ownership are directly visible. Inspected toolbar construction does not issue filesystem, database, network, subprocess, or IPC operations; commands/telemetry are action-run behavior unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu extension content and selection frequency affect cost, but no increased invocation count is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Invalidations correspond to existing rebuild/content-change events, rather than introducing repeated reconstruction or external boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and scroll +/- indicators in side-by-side, inline, and embedded notebook diffs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing line-decoration rendering and inline deleted-margin creation produce signs; browser style resolution and rasterization must complete for visible diff frames. Notebook diff widgets use the same DiffEditorWidget and enable indicators.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Style and rasterize diff-sign glyphs, replacing whole-element opacity with alpha in the pseudo-element glyph color.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same existing sign elements and glyphs; one matching color rule per glyph. No extra signs, per-sign JS work, or renderer requests are introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing signs were dimmed through opacity:0.7 on their containing element. The new rule dims the existing pseudo-element glyph with color-mix instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Rasterization remains part of frame rendering. Removing whole-element opacity avoids its grouping requirement without adding live filters or geometry reads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible decorated lines in normal editors; deleted view lines created for inline hunks; instantiated notebook cell diff widgets. The CSS change does not increase any of these cardinalities.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing renderer/main-thread style and browser raster/compositor scheduling; no new explicit IPC, subprocess, filesystem, database, network, or task issuance.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new application cache, retained collection, or DOM allocation. Existing viewport decoration output and inline view-zone ownership remain unchanged; the new glyph color follows currentColor through normal browser style handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that DOM cardinality, execution frequency, and external boundaries are unchanged; precise raster savings are not established by this static review.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact opacity-layer/raster behavior and savings depend on the browser and GPU backend. The PR's measurements were not independently reproduced, so a separate compositor regression-fix signal was not inferred from CSS alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence introduced performance regression. The changed rule adds no repeated JS/layout work, new retained state, or expensive external boundary. Merge editor gutter search hits resolve to a separate unchanged implementation and are not affected by this gutter cache.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all four changed files and all diff pages against base ae408942391f7d999284da20f4deef16a369ea1d. Traced scrolling, construction/resize/reveal, selection/menu updates, and indicator rendering including notebook embedding. No high-confidence introduced performance findings. Recorded the concrete synchronous-layout regression fix with introducing commit b7d35c8bdddeb7d4bfebf81cb6733b4a5ee06aa9. Static read-only review; runtime performance magnitudes were not independently measured.
